findings.title: Slice removes `k_first`, violating the plan's "no regression on k-first path" exit criterion
findings.description: The slice plan entry (140-slices.simulation-scaling.md:56) assigns three exit criteria, one of which is "no regression on k-first path." The design removes `k_first` entirely (lines 34, 67, 177–179, 199), which makes that criterion impossible to satisfy by construction. The design's rationale — that `k_first` becomes strictly worse once coherent reads land and is a "behavioral landmine" — is defensible, but the slice plan entry still names k-first preservation as a gate. Either the plan entry must be updated to drop that criterion (and authorize the removal) or the slice must retain a k-first path through the transition. As written, the design silently discards an assigned exit criterion. Recommendation: reconcile the plan entry with the design's mode-set change before implementation, since the final-commit default flip (line 349) depends on it.

findings.title: `radius_only` mode addition is scope beyond the plan entry's stated scope
findings.description: The slice plan entry frames slice 152 as a coherent-grid performance fix for k-nearest neighbor selection. The design adds a complete second neighbor mode — `radius_only` — with its own inner-loop specialization (lines 68, 181–183), config/`Workload` plumbing (lines 67, 349), a new measurement baseline (criterion 3, lines 357, 383–387), and repoints the load-bearing exit gate from "within 20% of k-first" to "within 20% of radius_only" (line 358). This is a real expansion of API surface and verification scope beyond what the plan assigns. The design's justification (radius_only is needed as the apples-to-apples comparison path against the published 16M reference, and as the metric/Reynolds mode) is well-argued, but the plan entry neither mentions `radius_only` nor authorizes a new mode. The added mechanism (one branch + one specialization) is lightweight, so the proportionality concern is bounded; the gap is authorization, not weight. Recommendation: confirm the plan entry is amended to scope in `radius_only` and the revised comparison baseline, or defer `radius_only` to a follow-up slice so this slice ships only the coherent reindex + k-nearest fix the plan describes.

findings.title: Coherent reindex, heap-semantics change, and writeback invariants are well-specified with failure modes
findings.description: The core mechanism — `coherent_reindex_kernel`, the inverse-permutation field for self-exclusion, the `heap_idx` coherent-slot semantics change, and the invariant that writebacks go to original-order fields while coherent fields are tick-scoped scratch — is specified with concrete code, data-flow diagrams, and clear invariants. The new I/O path (reindex kernel) has its failure modes enumerated: reindex cost domination at small N (risk 1, line 424), inverse-permutation scattered-read cost (risk 2, line 426), heap slot-vs-original-ID confusion (risk 3, line 428), and allocation-order interactions (risk 4, line 430), each with a mitigation. Synchronization between reindex and force kernel is handled via kernel-boundary temporal separation, consistent with the `graph=True` discipline used by the rest of the fused-tick pipeline (slices 143–149).

findings.title: NFR targets and memory budget are restated with specific numbers consistent with the architecture
findings.description: The design restates the performance target (k_nearest TPS at N=200k within 20% of the reference path, on the dev-class CUDA box per slice 145's protocol) and the parity NFR (mean speed, mean NN distance within 5% of numpy reference), both matching the slice plan entry. Memory cost is computed concretely (5.6 MB at N=200k, line ~"Memory cost at N=200k") and checked against the architecture's 320 MB working-set budget at N=2M. f32 dtype is preserved across all new fields, consistent with the architecture's f32-on-GPU Tier 2+ commitment. CUDA is the validation substrate, consistent with the architecture's CUDA-primary tier-gate principle.

`radius_only` mode addition is scope beyond the plan entry's stated scope
Coherent reindex, heap-semantics change, and writeback invariants are well-specified with failure modes
